reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure and every real polynomial p, let gamma=stdGaussian(E) be the actual centered standard Gaussian on E, let f(w,x)=p.eval(inner_product(w,x)), and let df(w,v,x)=p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x), for all w,v,x in E. There exist a single family hf proving MemLp(f(w,.),2,gamma) for every w, a single family hdf proving MemLp(df(w,v,.),2,gamma) for every w,v, and a map D assigning each w an actual continuous real linear operator D(w):E->L2(gamma), with the following properties. For every w,v, D(w)(v)=(hdf(w,v)).toLp(df(w,v,.)), an equality of the actual L2 classes. For every w in all E, F(u)=(hf(u)).toLp(f(u,.)) has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at w. There also exist real constants M1>0 and M2>0, fixed uniformly for all the subsequent parameters, such that for every w with norm_E(w)<=1, norm_op(D(w))<=M1; and for every w,u with norm_E(w)<=1 and norm_E(u)<=1, norm_op(D(u)-D(w))<=M2*norm_E(u-w). Here all derivative norms and derivative differences are operator norms of continuous real linear maps into L2(gamma), not norms of one selected direction or pointwise raw functions. The derivative limit is norm_{L2(gamma)}(F(w+h)-F(w)-D(w)(h))/norm_E(h)->0 as arbitrary nonzero ambient h tends to zero; this differentiability is global in w, including at and outside the unit-ball boundary. The boundedness and Lipschitz estimates are restricted to the closed unit ball, not merely its unit sphere. All memberships, derivative operators, differentiability, and positive constants are conclusions rather than supplied analytic premises. Membership entails almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm of the displayed functions, while toLp gives their actual equivalence classes under gamma. Proof choices do not change these classes. M1 and M2 may depend on the fixed E and p, with gamma fixed by E; they do not depend on w,u or a direction v. No dimension-independent or polynomial-independent bound, explicit formula, or sharpness of the constants is asserted. Positive M1,M2 need not be minimal and are compatible with an identically zero derivative. The hypotheses impose no polynomial degree or sign restriction and no nonzero-polynomial or positive-dimensionality assumption.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; real polynomial p and its actual derivative polynomial; fixed standard Gaussian gamma; raw functions f(w,x) and df(w,v,x); global L2 proof families hf,hdf; actual L2-class map F; continuous-linear derivative assignment D; and strictly positive real constants M1,M2 controlling D on the closed unit ball.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. p:Polynomial R is arbitrary, gamma=stdGaussian(E), and all w,u,v,h,x range over E. f and df take real values in their raw input variable x. F:E->Lp R 2 gamma. D:E->(E->L[R]Lp R 2 gamma) has continuous real linear operator values with the operator norm. M1,M2:R. The estimate domain is {w:E | norm(w)<=1}; both arguments of the Lipschitz bound lie in that same closed ball. No positive dimension is required; completeness of E follows from finite dimensionality over R.
quantifiers: For every E with the stated structures and every p, let gamma,f,df be fixed as displayed. There exist hf:forall w, MemLp(f(w,.),2,gamma), hdf:forall w,v, MemLp(df(w,v,.),2,gamma), and one D:E->(E->L[R]Lp R 2 gamma). These witnesses satisfy both the universal class identity for all w,v and Frechet differentiability at every w. In the same scope there exist M1,M2:R with both strictly positive, such that a single M1 bounds every D(w) for norm(w)<=1 and a single M2 bounds every operator difference for all w,u in the closed unit ball. Constants are chosen after E,p,D and before the universally quantified estimate arguments; they are not chosen separately for each pair of points.
assumptions: Only the displayed real inner-product normed, finite-dimensional and Borel measurable-space structures on E, and an arbitrary given real polynomial p. Gaussian square integrability of both f and df, construction of D, differentiability, positive constants, boundedness, and operator-norm Lipschitz control are all produced conclusions. The norm restrictions in the two estimate implications select their domain; they do not restrict the globally quantified differentiability or operator formula. No prior integrability, scalar-curve derivative, norm estimate, nonzero polynomial, positive degree, sign, or positive-dimensionality premise is given.
conclusion: There are global hf,hdf and D with D(w)(v)=[x->p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x)] in L2(gamma) for all w,v, and F(w)=[x->p.eval(inner_product(w,x))] has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w. There exist strictly positive M1,M2 such that norm_op(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and norm_op(D(u)-D(w))<=M2*norm_E(u-w) for all pairs in that ball. In particular the derivative assignment is Lipschitz, hence continuous, on that specified ball in the operator-norm topology.
scopes: The Gaussian gamma is fixed for all raw functions, quotient classes and derivative target norms. toLp forms the actual almost-everywhere class, so an arbitrary selected representative need match a raw function only gamma-almost everywhere. The D(w)(v) formula is a class identity for every ambient direction v. Each D(w) is genuinely linear and continuous in v; the additional M2 estimate concerns variation of the operator with the base point in the closed unit ball. Frechet differentiability uses arbitrary full-space increments, with no within-set or single-direction restriction, even when the base point has norm 1. Only the two uniform estimates are restricted to the ball, including its origin and boundary. The norms of D(w) and D(u)-D(w) are operator norms, taking all direction vectors into account. Their estimates imply corresponding bounds on values at any direction, but no particular direction is selected in the statement. Positive constants are not asserted optimal and allow zero derivative. Zero-dimensional E is permitted, in which case the ball contains its unique point and the operator estimates are trivially compatible with any positive constants. No parameter probability laws, label, loss functional, or scalar averaging integral appears.
constant_dependencies: M1 and M2 are existential finite real constants with M1>0,M2>0. They are uniform in w,u within the fixed radius-1 ball and in directions v through the operator norm. Their choice may depend on E,p and the fixed derivative assignment, whose mathematical class values are determined by the displayed formulas and are independent of membership proofs; gamma is fixed by E. No dimension-free, polynomial-uniform, explicit coefficient, optimality, or extension of these uniform bounds to all E is asserted. The raw derivative formula has exactly p.derivative.eval(inner_product(w,x))*inner_product(v,x), with no extra numerical factor or normalization.
